text:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx + streaming disconnects observed on /v1/stream in prod-eu-central. 5xx rate ~5.3% over 5m (alert threshold 1.25%). paging oncall.

maya (oncall): acknowledged, joining. throwing up traces and request samples. @sam can you pull the gateway access logs?

sam (eng-runtime): grabbing them now. quick glance: a cluster of 502/504s and client connection resets all concentrated on backend host-7. Many of the failed requests show `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` in the request/response path.

jo (eng-sre): p99 start latency jumped from 90ms -> 1.1s. Several clients report truncated streams / early EOF. monitoring shows spike in `upstream prematurely closed connection` coming from nginx-proxy.

lee (infra): checking host-7: kernel dmesg shows `tcp: too many orphaned sockets` and a NIC driver reload event around the window. NIC counters show rx_missed high. Forwarding to hardware vendor for investigation but we should mitigate traffic away from host-7 ASAP.

maya (oncall): customer impact: about 4% of live streaming sessions impacted; a handful of enterprise customers reported partial outputs. CS notified and holding external comms until we have a mitigation.

sam (eng-runtime): no deploys in the time window. Runtime logs show repeated `kv-cache` lock contention then some worker processes restarting on host-7. suspect combined kernel/NIC flakiness causing abrupt connection closes.

jo (eng-sre): relevant gateway log excerpt:

```
2026-03-14T10:12:03Z error: upstream closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.9.23, request: "POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.2.3.7:8080/", host: api.prod
2026-03-14T10:12:04Z warn: recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
```

sam (eng-runtime): mitigation proposal:
- Drain host-7 from streaming LB pool and mark as unschedulable for stream workloads
- Increase gateway keepalive and proxy timeout from 60s -> 120s to reduce mid-stream aborts from slow backends
- Enable per-customer routing fallback: switch affected enterprise customers to polling (non-stream) endpoint automatically for the next 30 minutes
- Temporarily disable chunked-response shim for model variant `rwd-stream-v3` to force un-chunked responses while we validate stability

lee (infra): executing drain: `kubectl label node host-7 redwood/drain=streaming` then removed host-7 from LB. Confirmed host-7 traffic dropped to zero for streaming routes.

sam (eng-runtime): toggled flag on `rwd-stream-v3`: `--feature-disable-chunked-shim` for the variant via config rollout; pushed config and restarted small fraction of pods.

jo (eng-sre): within 6 minutes of drain and config changes, 5xx rate reduced from 5.3% -> 1.4% and truncated-stream reports dropped significantly. p95 latency back to ~260ms.

maya (oncall): live mitigation looks good. Actions for immediate handoff: @sam you are incident lead, @jo continue monitoring, @lee pursue vendor escalation and collection of NIC/kernel artifacts. I'll be offline in 30m. If error rate exceeds 2% re-alert.

sam (eng-runtime): acknowledged, taking lead. collecting artifacts from host-7 now. please grab: dmesg, /proc/net/softnet_stat, ethtool -S, and container logs for runtime.

lee (infra): collected outputs and uploaded to S3: `s3://redwood-incident-logs/1855006789/`. snippets:

```
dmesg tail:
[Mar 14 10:11:59] kernel: tcp: too many orphaned sockets
[Mar 14 10:12:01] kernel: igbvf: module unload, driver reset

/ proc/net/softnet_stat:
00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000

ethtool -S eno4:
rx_missed=4123 tx_aborted=7 rx_errors=6
```

sam (eng-runtime): runtime logs show worker restarts and some OOM-adjacent messages. I'm attaching run of `journalctl -u redwood-runtime` to the S3 bundle.

dave (support): ACME customer opened a ticket with truncated responses. We offered a polling fallback URL and they accepted. CS will follow up for credits if SLA is impacted.

maya (oncall): incident severity provisional: Sev2 (partial customer-facing degradation). We'll finalize after RCA.

jo (eng-sre): suggested long-term fixes:
- gateway circuit-breaker for backends that return >15% premature-close over 3m for streaming routes -> mark backend unhealthy for streaming for 10m
- runtime: detect incomplete chunked frames and emit a final truncation token so clients get a clean end-of-stream instead of hanging
- infra: add NIC driver monitoring alert for rx_missed > 1000/min and kernel orphaned sockets > threshold

sam (eng-runtime): on runbook items: add a quickplay to force non-chunked path for canary traffic, and update autoscaler to avoid concentrating too many stream sessions on single node.

lee (infra): vendor confirmed intermittent VF/NIC driver crash in that kernel version; they provided a patched driver we can test on a staging host. Planning controlled kernel+driver upgrade with rollback steps.

maya (oncall): handoff note: I'm stepping out for 35m. @sam you'll continue as incident lead. Please escalate to Sev1 if errors reappear or customer impact increases.

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handover maya -> sam at 10:25 UTC. Next rotation: jo at 11:00 UTC.

sam (eng-runtime): documenting mitigation steps and artifacts in incident tracker `/incidents/1855006789`. upload contains: host-7-dmesg.log, host-7-ethtool.log, gateway-proxy.log, runtime-rwd-stream-v3.log, support-ACME-ticket-12345.txt.

jo (eng-sre): monitoring shows no recurrence after 45m. keeping watches for 2h. adding new alert `streaming.premature_closes_rate` firing if sustained >0.5% for 5m.

maya (oncall): closing live mitigation portion for now. Will write timeline and draft initial postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
